claim_en: THE NIGHT WINDOW AND THE ONE-WAY ALTAR: The limbs are placed at sunset and burn all night; day-pieces (the fistful, incense, frankincense, wood, the priests' and libation meal-offerings) ride up at night through the comprehensive 'law of the olah'; 'until the morning' is freed to the ash removal — its window is the whole night. And the altar is ONE-WAY: what is fit, once up, does not come down — R. Yehoshua classing by fire-fitness, R. Gamliel by altar-fitness (their recorded delta: unfit blood and libations), R. Shimon's principle sealing it: the courtyard accepts what became unfit INSIDE it (overnight, gone-out, tamei, wrong time or place, unfit handlers stay up; night-slaughter, spille...
middah: plain (the night window — limbs placed at sunset burn all night, the day-pieces riding the comprehensive 'law of the burnt offering'; 'until the morning' freed to the ash removal, M-18, beside; the one-way altar's recorded three-way)

claim_en: THE CONSECRATING SURFACES: The altar consecrates what is appropriate to it (Exod 29:37); the RAMP is included; the ministering vessels consecrate what is appropriate to them (Exod 30:29) — and the vessels are TYPED: wet consecrates wet, dry measures dry, never across; a punctured vessel consecrates only while it still performs its whole-function; all of it inside the courtyard only.
middah: plain (the consecrating surfaces — the altar and the ramp (Exod 29:37), the vessels typed wet and dry (Exod 30:29), inside the courtyard only)

claim_en: ONE FIRE SOURCE: The inner incense altar's fire is kindled from the outer altar ('the fire of the altar shall be kindled thereby'); the menorah's rides the continuous-fire clause with Exod 27:20; the Yom Kippur coal pan's is sealed by Lev 16:12 — 'from off the altar BEFORE the LORD': the altar which is partly, not wholly, before the LORD is the outer one. The whole fire topology drains from one source.
middah: plain (one fire source — the inner altar's fire from the outer clause; the lamp by Exod 27:20; the coal pan sealed by 'from off the altar before the LORD' read as the outer altar, the context read, I12, beside)

claim_en: THE ASH-LIFTING PROTOCOL: The linen garment is cut to his SIZE; the linen spec runs byssus, new, six-stranded, worn with no other garments (Rebbi: even worn ones valid — the recorded three-way on what 'shall put on' adds); breeches directly on the flesh, nothing interposing, nothing before them. The ashes lifted are the innermost consumed coals — not wood-ash, not limbs — placed gently, all, unscattered, beside the altar; unconsumed limbs return to the altar's sides; a limb that sprang off before midnight is returned and still carries sacrilege liability — the fire's claim runs to midnight.
middah: plain (the ash-lifting protocol — the linen cut to his size, the keyword 'his measure', M-09, beside; the innermost coals; the fire's claim to midnight)

claim_en: THE CARRYING GARMENTS: 'Other garments' for taking the ashes out are likened to the ones taken off — CONSECRATED, but lesser in value; R. Elazar reads 'others': blemished priests, unfit for the services, are kasher for the ash-carrying — it is not a priestly service proper.
middah: plain ('other garments' likened to the ones taken off — consecrated but lesser; R. Elazar's blemished priests fit for the carrying)

claim_en: THE PERPETUAL FIRE MACHINE: Extinguishing the altar fire is a NEGATIVE COMMANDMENT; kindling happens on top of the altar; a sustenance pile feeds the flame. The morning runs on a PRECEDENCE ALGORITHM read off the doubled 'in the morning': the two logs precede the daily offering, the wood precedes the incense, the lamps precede the incense; the great pile carries every offering. THE DAY BRACKET: nothing precedes the morning tamid, nothing follows the afternoon tamid — 'the completers.' 'Continuous' overrides the Sabbath and tumah; on the journeys the fire is kept — R. Yehudah inverting a vessel over it, R. Shimon carrying it on a pan (dual-track); and the wood-pile COUNT is a recorded nume...
middah: plain (extinguishing a negative commandment; the morning precedence algorithm read off the doubled 'in the morning', E10, beside; the day bracket; the journeys' dual track; the wood-pile count a recorded number)

claim_en: THE MEAL-OFFERING INTAKE: ONE LAW for all meal-offerings: oil and frankincense even for the wholly-burnt (the priests' own); Temple as tabernacle; no bamah. Presentation: fit only, all at once, the sons not the daughters; and the CORNER ALGORITHM — 'before the LORD' intersected with 'in front of the altar' resolves to the SOUTHWEST corner, R. Eliezer naming the resolution rule: prefer the reading that satisfies both verses. The fistful: one tenth-measure in ONE vessel, no vessel for the fist, no neighbor's flour or oil, the frankincense present in the vessel at the taking, then picked out and smoked.
middah: plain (one law for all meal offerings; the corner algorithm — 'before the LORD' intersected with 'in front of the altar' resolves to the southwest, R. Eliezer's prefer-both-verses rule, I13, beside; the fistful's vessel rules)

claim_en: THE REMAINDER LAWS: Only a VALID offering's remainder is eaten; the multiplied eating-verbs permit any manner and allow mundane food and terumah alongside it WHEN INSUFFICIENT (never when ample); eating it unleavened is a MITZVAH — the permitted-forbidden-permitted ladder does not restore the original permission without the written command; even a surviving part is eaten; the place is the courtyard, including chambers on mundane ground that open into the holy.
middah: plain (only a valid offering's remainder; the multiplied eating-verbs, E10, permit any manner and mundane food alongside when insufficient; unleavened a commandment; the courtyard's chambers)

claim_en: LEAVEN AND APPORTIONMENT: 'Shall not be BAKED leavened' singles baking out to teach PER-OPERATION liability — kneading and rolling each liable in themselves. Apportionment waits for the fire: the priests divide only after the fistful is consigned (all offerings, through 'holy of holies'); the unfit is not divided; premature division does not unfit. The double comparison: like the sin-offering — from mundane money, by day, with the right hand; like the guilt-offering — a fistful taken not-for-its-sake stays FIT; R. Shimon partitions instead: the sinner's offering follows the sin-offering rule, the gift the guilt-offering rule (dual-track).
middah: I8 ('shall not be baked leavened' singles baking out to teach per-operation liability; the double comparison to the sin and guilt offerings, M-03, beside; R. Shimon's partition)

claim_en: TOUCH AND SHARE: 'Every male' includes the blemished FOR APPORTIONMENT; the statute spans the Temple and the generations; eating follows the fire-offering. Touch-sanctification requires ABSORPTION ('in them'); partial contact taints the touched part only — it is cut away; what touches becomes LIKE the offering: unfit if unfit, eaten under its stringencies if fit.
middah: E1 ('every male' includes the blemished for apportionment; touch-sanctification requires absorption; what touches becomes like the offering)

source: Onkelos Leviticus 6:13; Sifra, Tzav, Chapter 5; Sifra, Tzav, Section 3
claim_en: THE PERPETUAL GRIDDLE OFFERING: The tenth-measure GATES SERVICE: a high priest or ordinary priest who served before bringing his investiture tenth — service INVALID. Anointing by day; never two high priests at once. THE HALVING INVARIANT: 'its half' means half of a WHOLE tenth — bring whole, divide, half at morning half at evening; a tamei evening half, or a successor priest mid-day, brings a NEW WHOLE and halves it (two halves offered, two lost — the recorded ledger). The measure is the data channel's own arithmetic: one-tenth of three se'im — seven quarters and a fraction — with Onkelos performing the conversion inside the verse ('one of ten in three se'im'). Succession: the son precede...
middah: plain (the perpetual griddle offering — the tenth-measure gates service, anointing by day, never two high priests; the halving invariant; the received translation of 6:13 the ink leg)

claim_en: THE GRIDDLE SPEC: The griddle is a ministering vessel; the oil quantity is DERIVED BY RESEMBLANCE: three logs per tenth-measure from the libation meal-offering — the recorded selection rule preferring the daily offering that overrides Sabbath and tumah (two more recorded routes to the same three logs; the two-log ram-route refuted by all-one-tenth likeness). 'Soaked' means scalded with hot oil to saturation — a THREE-SEAT CENSUS: no other soaked offering in the Torah but this, the thanksgiving bread, and the investiture bread. Brought before the libations; the baking verb carries a recorded three-way (lightly / beautifully / many); folding: the high priest's to two, the ordinary priest's ...
middah: plain (the griddle a ministering vessel; the oil quantity derived by resemblance to the libation meal offering, M-03, beside; 'soaked' scalded — a three-seat census, ink, beside; the baking verb's three-way)

claim_en: THE PRIEST'S OWN MEAL-OFFERING: Never eaten — but the priest's DAUGHTER's is eaten (the class boundary runs on the priest, not the priestly line); his gift offering included; even part liable; the doubled 'entire' (kalil) cross-applies whole-smoking and the eating ban between 6:15 and 6:16; R. Eliezer: everything under 'entire' adds a negative commandment for eating.
middah: plain (the priest's own meal offering never eaten, his daughter's eaten — the class boundary on the priest; the doubled 'entire', E10, cross-applies the whole-smoking and the eating ban)

claim_en: THE SIN-OFFERING'S LAW: ONE LAW for all sin-offerings: the blood-on-garment WASHING reaches even the inner burnt ones (the a-fortiori that would exempt them defeated); the BIRD offering excluded — its pinching is not slaughter; every sin-offering slaughtered NORTH (with R. Eliezer's fixed-olah derivation and the communal peace-offerings included); the eater is the offering-priest class, excluding the day-immersed, the atonement-lacking, and the mourner; and the blood belongs ABOVE — applied below it does not atone: the 'it' exclusion holds against the one-application leniency and the inner-blood counter.
middah: plain (one law for all sin offerings — the washing reaches the inner ones, the exempting a-fortiori defeated, I1 refuted, beside; the bird excluded, E2; the north; the eater class; the blood above; the received translation of 6:19 the ink leg)

claim_en: THE WASHING MACHINE: Washing rides FIT blood — with the recorded three-way on blood unfitted later (R. Akiva's time-of-fitness criterion against R. Shimon's never); only ITS blood (not neighbors', not broth); only the SPOT; and the SPRINKLE-FITNESS criterion sorts the case table: from the hand before sprinkling — wash; after — no; spilled from the vessel and gathered — wash; from the neck or off the horn and base — no. Garment scope is a recorded dispute (tumah-capable vs implement). Washing happens IN THE HOLY PLACE, and the juxtaposition extends the venue to the breaking and scouring; the ruled RETURN TABLE: garment out — returned and washed inside; tamei outside — torn, returned, washe...
middah: plain (the washing machine — fit blood with the recorded three-way, its blood, the spot, the sprinkle-fitness case table; the venue extended to breaking and scouring by juxtaposition, E28, beside; the return table)

claim_en: THE VESSEL PURGE: Earthenware (alum-crystal vessels included) BREAKS — cooked in or hot-poured alike; copper stands for ALL METALS and SCOURS AND RINSES — repeated cookings, one purge at the end (R. Tarfon's festival window against the sages' eating-time, dual-track); scour within, rinse without; the rinse water: any amount, water only, any water. The purge rides offerings with a FIT phase (R. Yaakov against R. Shimon — the same criterion pair as the washing); 'every male' closes the blemish ladder at PERMANENT blemishes; and the TASTE THRESHOLD: mixtures where the stringent imparts taste are eaten under its stringencies — below it, no touch-unfitness and no purge.
middah: plain (the vessel purge — earthenware breaks, copper for all metals scours and rinses; the fit-phase criterion; 'every male' closing the blemish ladder, E1, beside; the taste threshold)

claim_en: THE ENTRY BOUNDARY: A sin-offering whose blood — even PART of it — enters the tent is not eaten but burned; the two-cups table (one out: the inner kasher; one in: R. Yossi Haglili keeps the outer fit against the sages, dual-track); the boundary is DIRECTIONAL — what enters unfits, what leaves does not ('into the tent of meeting'); it holds at Shiloh and the Temple; whether ENTRY alone unfits or only atonement made inside is the recorded R. Eliezer / R. Shimon dispute (unwitting entry kasher on the second view). Burning is in the holy place, extended to all invalidated higher-order offerings; and the tamei-flesh BURN-LOCATION matrix is carried in four recorded resolutions — Beth Shammai an...
middah: plain (the entry boundary — blood even in part entering the tent, E1, beside, burns the offering; directional; the R. Eliezer and R. Shimon dispute; the burn-location matrix)
